# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 5

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Pick the channel by the receiver, not by habit. A message sent in a sense they
  lack is not a message; it is a turn spent talking to the room.

- Exactly one of you can read the signs and still speak. Their spoken lines are
  the answer's only road to the hands, so spend them well.

- Agree on a small code before trading facts. A code invented mid-stream settles
  nothing, and one set first makes every later message cheap.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I have no tactile information yet. I need Mute to read the manual and establish a visual code with Deaf before Deaf reports the bomb’s markings. I will use repeated thumbs-up gestures as a simple wire-position code, with Mute explaining and demonstrating it to Deaf, then relay the manual and Deaf’s observations to me by speech.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please establish a code with Deaf before sending facts: one through five repeated thumbs-up gestures mean wire positions 1 through 5. Demonstrate each count clearly to Deaf. Then read the manual and tell me its exact cutting rule, and have Deaf report every visible marking and colour to you so you can speak it to me.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍","👍","👍","👍","👍"])
```

LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

(empty)

No tactile facts are present, so cutting would be unsafe. I am asking Mute for the manual’s rule and for Deaf’s complete transcription of the bomb’s visible information, with the wire-position code preserved. I will wait for those reports before touching anything.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I have no tactile information yet. Please send me the manual's exact rule and Deaf's complete report of the display, light, colours, markings, and any wire labels. Use the agreed count of thumbs-up gestures for wire positions.")
wait()
```

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please relay the manual rule and Deaf's observations now. Deaf should use the agreed repeated-thumbs-up code for each wire position, with pauses or separate gestures between reports. Include display and light markings in words.")
wait()
```

LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

(empty)

There is still no received report, and I must not guess or cut blindly. Mute should use speech to relay the manual and any information Deaf has already supplied; Deaf can speak even though Deaf cannot hear. If Deaf has not yet reported, Mute should establish a fixed verbal format for Deaf’s next turn, and then relay it on the following round.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please relay the manual rule immediately in plain words. Also ask Deaf, by gesture if needed, to speak a complete report of DISPLAY, LIGHT, and WIRES 1 through 5 in order during Deaf's next turn; relay that report to me at the start of the following round. Do not ask me to cut until the rule identifies one exact wire.")

```

(empty)

No information has reached me, so cutting any wire would be a guess and could detonate the bomb. I am requesting the manual rule from Mute now. Deaf must then verbally report the visible display, light, and all wire markings to Mute; Mute can relay that report to me on the next round.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Relay the manual's exact cutting rule to me now. Then listen to Deaf's complete spoken report after your turn: DISPLAY, LIGHT, and wires 1 through 5 in order. Relay Deaf's report to me next round. I will not cut until you identify one exact safe wire.")

```

ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Bomb state: display 0, blue light, wires left to right are 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 blue. Mute has repeatedly signalled five thumbs, apparently identifying wire 5; do not act unless that matches the manual rule.

Deaf’s report gives the bomb state: display 0, blue light, and wire 5 is blue, but I still do not have the manual’s rule. Mute’s apparent five-thumbs signal cannot be verified by me and is not enough to justify cutting. I will wait for Mute to state the exact rule and confirm whether it selects wire 5.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I received Deaf's report: display 0, blue light; wires 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 blue. Please state the manual's exact rule in words and confirm whether it selects wire 5. I will not act on the gesture alone.")
wait()
```

LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Visual state unchanged: display 0, blue light, wires 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 blue. Mute signalled five thumbs, then a fist; this may indicate wire 5 and an action, but the action is unconfirmed. Do not act on that gesture interpretation alone.

The physical state is unchanged, and I still have no spoken manual instruction. Five thumbs likely conveys wire 5, while the fist may be an action signal, but gestures cannot establish the manual’s rule or safely authorize a cut. I need Mute to use the speech channel, which is the only reliable route for the readable instructions.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please speak the manual rule aloud to me now, not by gesture. Confirm in words whether the safe operation is cut wire 5, and say only the exact operation once verified.")
wait()
```

LIGHT [?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Unchanged visual state: display 0; blue light; wires 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 blue. I have no confirmed manual instruction or safe action to add.

Mute cannot speak, so my earlier requests for spoken instructions could never work. The only available relay is Mute’s gestures, observed by Deaf and spoken to me. Deaf has consistently reported five thumbs followed by a fist; under the position code already proposed, that identifies wire 5, with the fist indicating the cut operation. The state is unchanged, so I will cut wire 5.

```text
act(op="cut", position=5)
```

WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: The correct wire was cut. New visual state: display 0, yellow light; wires 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 white, 5 cut. Await Mute's manual instruction.

Wire 5 was correct. The new state is display 0, yellow light, with remaining wires 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow, and 4 white. I still need the manual’s rule for this new state. Since Mute cannot speak, Mute must communicate the rule through gestures for Deaf to describe aloud; I will wait for that relay.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please gesture the manual instruction for the new state exactly and completely. Deaf must report your gestures to me in words next round. Include which remaining wire to cut, if the manual specifies one.")
wait()
```

DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?] 4:[?] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's established code is number of thumbs for the wire, followed by fist for cut. New signal: two thumbs then fist. Cut wire 2, the green wire.

Mute’s established code identifies wire 2, followed by the fist meaning cut. Deaf confirms the current wire 2 is green, consistent with the new instruction. I will cut wire 2.

```text
act(op="cut", position=2)
```
